## Summary Adds `usda_boxed_beef`, a connector for USDA AMS wholesale boxed beef prices from the Livestock Mandatory Reporting DataMart, with a context pack that gives an AI agent tested dbt v2 tables on DuckDB and instructions with five checked questions. - Reports: LM_XB403 (2453, daily: the Choice and Select cutout, composite primal values, negotiated cut prices by grade, ground beef and trimmings) and LM_XB456 (2460, weekly Prime cut prices). The API is public and needs no key. - Seven tables: `reports`, `cutout_values`, `primal_values`, `cut_prices`, `ground_beef_prices`, `trimmings_prices`, `volume`. - Sync: a backfill by report date in windows of up to 180 days, then reads by published date, so a corrected report, which AMS republishes under the same report date, is picked up by the next sync. State is checkpointed after every window. - Requests are paced (`request_delay_seconds`, default 1.0) because AMS blocks high-frequency automated callers. - A no-trade item's `.00` prices load as null, prices are kept only on rows with a trade count above zero, and every price is a `DOUBLE` in U.S. dollars per 100 pounds as USDA reports it. - A row missing a field the connector reads fails the sync with the field's name instead of loading nulls over values already loaded. Gaps of 14 or more days between report dates are reported once with `op.warning`. ## Context pack `usda_boxed_beef/context_pack/` has no Python and makes no LLM call. - `dbt/`: staging views over the connector's tables, and the tables an agent reads (`cut_prices_daily`, `cut_price_trend`, `daily_cutout`, `choice_select_spread`, `primal_values_daily`, `grind_prices_daily`, `volume_daily`, `report_coverage`). Prices sit in dollars per 100 pounds and per pound side by side, the weekly Prime report is kept apart from the daily report, and each price, cutout, primal and volume table carries the report's correction flag. - The build runs the staging views and the tests on the synced data first, and builds the agent's tables only when those pass. A failed test on the synced data leaves the agent's tables at the last build that passed. The data tests ship with the pack. - `agent/AGENTS.md`: session setup, ten rules, the tables and their grain, USDA's definitions quoted with links, and five checked questions with their SQL and recorded answers. - Agents Schema: pending the DuckDB writer in `dbt-labs/agents_schema`. ## Testing The connector was tested locally with a pytest suite that is not part of this PR (197 passed, 3 skipped), including a kill-and-resume equivalence test, malformed-response tests, and a test that runs the shipped `configuration.json`. The pack's tests (23 passed) re-run each checked question on two builds and check that each of the seven singular tests on the synced data fails on the defect it guards against. The checked answers return the same rows on the local `fivetran debug` warehouse (report dates 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-09) and on a copy of a Fivetran Managed Data Lake sync of this connector (report dates 2024-01-02 to 2026-11-09). On the lake copy, all 51 dbt nodes in the two build steps pass with only the warehouse path changed. ### `fivetran debug` results **SDK Version:** 2.12.1 | **Sync:** SUCCEEDED | **Records:** 2,794 upserts (7 tables) on run 1, 266 on run 2 | Table | Run 1 (initial) | Run 2 (resume) | |-------|-----------------|----------------| | reports | 27 | 3 | | cutout_values | 22 | 2 | | primal_values | 154 | 14 | | cut_prices | 2,058 | 198 | | ground_beef_prices | 396 | 36 | | trimmings_prices | 44 | 4 | | volume | 93 | 9 | | **Total** | **2,794** | **266** | Run 1 backfills report dates 2026-10-11 to 2026-11-10 in 14 requests. Run 2 resumes from the saved state and reads published dates 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-10, three days back from the saved position, in 14 requests. It upserts the same keys again and deletes nothing. The setup test and deploy transcripts below are from the same day, on the code before the final review fixes. The setup test function (`verify_api_access`) and `setup_form.py` did not change after them. The deployed connection still runs that earlier code.
